title: Slack and binding rows of a fleet plan

blocks.text: A city transit agency plans next year's bus purchases with a small MILP, and its board wants a report of the rules the chosen plan sits on. The agency's model is stored as data: each row is a `Row` with a name, its coefficients by variable, a sense (`"<="`, `">="` or `"=="`) and a right-hand side. A plan gives each variable a value; a variable the plan does not mention is 0.

items: `slack(row, plan)`: the room the plan leaves on the row, $`\ge 0`$ when the row holds, $`0`$ when the plan sits exactly on it, and negative when the plan breaks it. An `==` row is broken by any miss, above or below.
`binding(rows, plan, tol=1e-6)`: the names of the rows the plan keeps with no room left, within `tol`, in the order given.

blocks.text: With $`a`$ a row's coefficients, $`x`$ the plan and $`b`$ its right-hand side, write the slack of each kind of row first, then code it:
\text{slack}(a^\top x \le b) = \;? \qquad \text{slack}(a^\top x \ge b) = \;? \qquad \text{slack}(a^\top x = b) = \;?

"Binding" here means what the board will read: the plan keeps the row and has no room left on it. A row the plan breaks is a different finding, and the tests check that it is not reported as binding. The tests use their own rows and plans; no solver is needed.

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from slacks import Row, binding, slack

rows = [
    Row("yard_bays", {"tram_x": 10, "tram_y": 8}, "<=", 50),
    Row("low_floor_min", {"tram_y": 1, "tram_z": 1}, ">=", 3),
    Row("depot_lease", {"lease": 1}, "==", 1),
]
plan = {"tram_x": 2, "tram_y": 2, "tram_z": 1, "lease": 1}

for row in rows:
    print(f"slack of {row.name}:", slack(row, plan))
print("binding rows:", binding(rows, plan))
print("binding rows, lease 0:", binding(rows, {**plan, "lease": 0}))

cases.says: a plan's slack on a capacity row, and the list of rows it leaves no room on
a >= row has positive slack when the plan is above its floor
an == row missed on either side has negative slack
a row the plan breaks is not reported as binding
a slack within the tolerance of zero counts as binding

origin.section: A Row Binds When the Plan Leaves It No Slack

concepts: a row binds when the plan keeps it with zero slack, within a tolerance
a row's slack is measured from the plan and the row's sense and bound, with no help from the solver
